name: Oregon
tagline: From the Columbia Gorge waterfalls to Crater Lake, the Steens and the Wallowas.
intro: Oregon's byways follow the coast on US 101, climb the Cascades past lava fields and crater lakes, run up the Columbia Gorge and the Wallowas, and cross the high desert of the Steens and the Outback. This chapter follows the Oregon Scenic Byways program of the Oregon Department of Transportation, which counts 29 routes in four tiers, from All-American Roads down to Oregon Tour Routes, a lower rank for shorter local drives that may include rough gravel; the program has been dormant since ODOT stopped taking new designations. Roads designated only by the Bureau of Land Management or the Forest Service are listed separately.

members.name: Historic Columbia River Highway Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Samuel Lancaster's 1913 road climbs from the Sandy River to Vista House on Crown Point, drops past Multnomah Falls and its 1925 lodge, and farther east sends walkers through the restored Mosier Twin Tunnels.

members.name: Hells Canyon Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 218-mile loop around the Wallowa Mountains from La Grande to Baker City, by way of Joseph and Wallowa Lake in the Nez Perce homeland, with a forest-road spur to the Hells Canyon Overlook above the Snake.

members.name: Pacific Coast Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 101 runs the whole Oregon shore from Astoria to the California line, past Haystack Rock at Cannon Beach, sea stacks and lighthouses, on beaches Oregon law keeps open to all. Gray whales pass from November to June.

members.name: Volcanic Legacy Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Diamond Lake Junction the byway climbs to the rim of Crater Lake, the caldera Mount Mazama left 7,700 years ago, then runs beside Upper Klamath Lake, Oregon's largest, on toward Lassen in California.

members.name: McKenzie Pass-Santiam Pass Scenic Byway
members.blurb: An 82-mile loop from Sisters over two Cascade passes. Old OR 242 crosses bare lava at McKenzie Pass, where the CCC built Dee Wright Observatory in 1935, and the return passes Clear Lake and Sahalie Falls.

members.name: West Cascades Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Starting at Office Bridge, Oregon's longest covered bridge, forest roads run north from Westfir along the Willamette's North Fork, the McKenzie, the North Santiam and the Clackamas. The high sections close from mid-November through April.

members.name: Rogue-Umpqua Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Long called the highway of waterfalls, the road follows the North Umpqua from Roseburg past Glide's Colliding Rivers and the CCC's Mott Bridge, climbs to Diamond Lake under Mount Thielsen, then comes down the Rogue.

members.name: Outback Scenic Byway
members.blurb: OR 31 leaves the pines near La Pine for sagebrush, passing Fort Rock, the marshes of Summer Lake and the 30-mile wall of Abert Rim before Lakeview, which at 4,800 feet calls itself Oregon's tallest town.

members.name: Cascade Lakes Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Century Drive, named for the hundred-mile dirt road it once was, climbs out of Bend past Mount Bachelor to a chain of lakes along the upper Deschutes. Beyond the ski area it closes all winter.

members.name: Mt. Hood Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Hood River the byway climbs OR 35 through pear and apple orchards, crosses Barlow Pass where Oregon Trail wagons topped the Cascades, and sends a spur up to the WPA's Timberline Lodge before US 26 descends to Troutdale.

members.name: Blue Mountain Scenic Byway
members.blurb: OR 74 leaves I-84 along Willow Creek, an Oregon Trail stopping place, through wheat towns to Heppner. Forest roads then cross the Umatilla National Forest by Ukiah, blue with camas in spring, to the North Fork John Day.

members.name: Elkhorn Drive Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 106-mile loop from Baker City through gold country, past the 1935 dredge at Sumpter and the old mining town of Granite, then over Elkhorn Summit at 7,392 feet to Anthony Lake and down to Haines.

members.name: Journey Through Time Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Biggs on the Columbia to Baker City, 286 miles through wheat country and the old wool town of Shaniko, past fossil beds at Clarno and the Kam Wah Chung museum of Chinese miners in John Day.

members.name: High Desert Discovery Scenic Byway
members.blurb: OR 205 runs south from Burns past the marshes of Malheur National Wildlife Refuge to Frenchglen and its 1920s hotel, then along Catlow Rim, where wild horses and bighorn are often in view, to Fields.

members.name: Over the Rivers & Through the Woods Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Brownsville, settled in 1846, the route passes Crawfordsville's covered bridge and the mill town of Sweet Home, then climbs the South Santiam beside the old Santiam Wagon Road to Tombstone Pass and Hackleman's old-growth grove.

members.name: Trees to Sea Scenic Byway
members.blurb: OR 6 climbs from Banks over the Coast Range through the Tillamook State Forest, replanted after the Tillamook Burn fires of 1933, past a replica fire lookout at the forest center and down through dairy pasture to Cape Meares.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: McKenzie River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Thirty-four miles of OR 126 up the McKenzie from the farmland east of Eugene, past the Leaburg dam with its art deco powerhouse and a 1907 fish hatchery kept as it was, to the forest at the Aufderheide Drive.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Umpqua River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the brick storefronts of Oakland the road follows the Umpqua through the Coast Range by Elkton's vineyards and a replica of the Hudson's Bay Company's Fort Umpqua, then past the elk pastures at Dean Creek to Reedsport.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Marys Peak to Pacific Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Corvallis and Philomath, OR 34 follows the Alsea River to the coast, with one side road built by the CCC up Marys Peak, at 4,097 feet the top of the Coast Range, and another to Alsea Falls.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Silver Falls Tour Route
members.blurb: A 55-mile drive from south of Salem past vineyards and Christmas tree farms to Silver Falls State Park, where a trail passes ten waterfalls and the CCC's 1941 lodge, then on to Silverton and the abbey town of Mount Angel.

members.name: Grande Tour Route
members.blurb: A loop out of La Grande around the Grande Ronde Valley, past the ruins of Hot Lake Resort, once a spa hospital, to Union and to Cove, whose Episcopal chapel dates from 1869, among cherry orchards and mint fields.

members.name: East Steens Tour Route
members.blurb: OR 78 leaves Burns for the sage flats, then gravel East Steens Road runs under the mountain's eastern wall, a vertical mile high, past Mann Lake and the salt flats of the Alvord Desert to the cafe at Fields.

members.name: Steens Loop Tour Route
members.blurb: From Frenchglen a gravel loop climbs nearly to 10,000 feet on Steens Mountain, to the rim of glacier-cut Kiger Gorge and the drop to the Alvord Desert, then descends through South Steens wild horse country. Closed in winter.

members.name: Diamond Loop Tour Route
members.blurb: Off OR 205 the loop crosses the south end of Malheur refuge to the ranch hamlet of Diamond and its hotel, then to Pete French's round barn, built for breaking horses in winter, and the lava domes of Diamond Craters.

members.name: Charleston to Bandon Tour Route
members.blurb: From the fishing port of Charleston out to Cape Arago, past Sunset Bay's sheltered beach and the Shore Acres gardens, then south on Seven Devils Road by South Slough and the cranberry bogs to Bandon's old town.
members.note: Shown on the map as Charleston-Bandon Loop Tour Route.

members.name: Myrtle Creek-Canyonville Tour Route
members.blurb: Up the South Umpqua from Canyonville past the Milo covered bridge to Tiller, over a narrow one-lane forest road to Red Top Pond, and down South Myrtle Creek to a covered bridge brought from Lane County.

members.name: Cow Creek Tour Route
members.blurb: Cow Creek Road leaves I-5 at Riddle, once a nickel-smelting town, and follows the creek and the 1869 Oregon and California rail grade through a wooded canyon where gold panning is allowed, back to I-5 at Glendale.

members.name: Cottage Grove Covered Bridge Tour Route
members.blurb: A 20-mile drive out of Cottage Grove past seven covered bridges, among them Mosby Creek, built in 1920 and the oldest in Lane County, the Dorena bridge by its reservoir, and the 1925 Chambers railroad bridge in town.

members.name: Vineyard and Valley Tour Route
members.blurb: Back roads of the Tualatin Valley from Sherwood to Hillsboro, past hazelnut groves and foothill vineyards and through farm settlements begun by Dutch, Scots and Swiss, with the white 1878 Old Scotch Church near the end.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Christmas Valley Back Country Byway
members.blurb: Ninety-three miles of county and BLM roads off OR 31 into the high desert around Christmas Valley, out to dunes of ash and pumice that blew in when Mount Mazama erupted some 7,000 years ago.

members.name: Galice to Hellgate Back Country Byway
members.blurb: A narrow paved road down the Rogue River canyon from Hellgate past the community of Galice and the visitor center at Rand to Grave Creek, where the Rogue River Trail, first walked by the Takelma, begins.

members.name: Grave Creek to Marial Back Country Byway
members.blurb: A slow one-lane climb above the Wild and Scenic Rogue from Grave Creek, past an overlook of Rainie Falls, through Siskiyou forest to the old Rogue River Ranch at Marial, with no services along the way.

members.name: Lakeview to Steens Back Country Byway
members.blurb: Out of Lakeview over the Warner Mountains and down to the Warner Valley lakes, rimmed on their north shores by crescent dunes, then up past Hart Mountain's pronghorn refuge with Steens Mountain on the far horizon.
members.note: Shown on the map as Lakeview to Steens Mountain Back Country Byway.

members.name: Lower Crooked River Back Country Byway
members.blurb: OR 27 runs 43 miles north from US 20 to Prineville, first on gravel through open range under basalt buttes, then across Bowman Dam's spillway into the Crooked River gorge and its riverside camps.

members.name: Lower Deschutes River Back Country Byway
members.blurb: Thirty-two miles along the east bank of the Lower Deschutes, paved out of Maupin to Sherars Falls and gravel beyond, beside rapids in a steep canyon, from Locked Gate to the campground at Macks Canyon.

members.name: Nestucca River Back Country Byway
members.blurb: A slow Coast Range road down the Nestucca River through rain forest that takes some 120 inches a year, past mossy sandstone cliffs and four riverside campgrounds, with log trucks to share the curves.

members.name: Quartzville Back Country Byway
members.blurb: Quartzville Road leaves US 20 east of Sweet Home and follows the Quartzville River past the swimming hole at Yellowbottom and gravel bars where recreational gold panning is still allowed.

members.name: Snake River-Mormon Basin Back Country Byway
members.blurb: About 150 miles of ranch and canyon roads in Baker and Malheur counties, along the Snake River above Brownlee Reservoir to Huntington, with Oregon Trail wagon ruts kept near the interpretive center outside Baker City.

members.name: South Fork John Day River Back Country Byway
members.blurb: Gravel road south from Dayville up the South Fork John Day through basalt canyons and ponderosa pine, past 56-foot Izee Falls and the two-room Izee schoolhouse, which taught its last pupils in 1989.

members.name: South Fork-Alsea River Back Country Byway
members.blurb: A short Coast Range road along the South Fork of the Alsea between the Alsea valley and Monroe, under Douglas fir and vine maple, with a stop where the river spills 30 feet at Alsea Falls.

members.name: Steens Mountain Back Country Byway
members.blurb: The BLM's name for the Steens Mountain Loop Road, climbing from Frenchglen to the gorge overlooks at Kiger, Big Indian and Little Blitzen and passing the Riddle Brothers' old ranch on the way down.

members.name: Rogue-Coquille Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Gold Beach the road follows the Wild and Scenic Rogue up to Agness, crosses through the Siskiyou National Forest to Powers, and comes down the Coquille valley to the town of Coquille.

members.name: State of Jefferson Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Named for the 1941 State of Jefferson movement, the byway runs from Yreka down the Klamath River to Happy Camp, then climbs over the 5,000-foot Grayback summit and comes down to O'Brien, just inside Oregon.

members.name: Emigrant Trail
members.blurb: Starting at New Pine Creek on the Oregon line, the route passes Goose Lake and its waterfowl, runs through Alturas and the Modoc National Forest, and ends at Tulelake, linking the Outback byway to California's volcanic roads.
